rows.rationale: Three-way match is exact on a GOODS PO (clause 1): 200 EACH ordered, received and invoiced at $4.20 each, no UOM difference and zero price variance (clauses 3-4). Tax recomputes to $63.00 at the vendor's 7.5% rate, matching the supplier exactly (clause 5). No non-PO lines and no open credit memos; $903.00 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

The only exception was unit-of-measure: the vendor billed 480 EACH @ $2.00 against a PO of 40 CASE @ $24.00, and at pack size 12 (vendor.json) these are identical ($960.00 net). Clause 2 makes that normalisation, not a defect. Receipt GR-7702 confirms 40 CASE received (clause 4, no variance), price is at PO (clause 3), and 7.5% tax recomputes to $72.00 exactly (clause 5). No credit memos; $1,032.00 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

Three-way match is complete on this GOODS PO: 100 EACH ordered, received and invoiced (clause 1, 4). The unit price of $63.10 against $62.00 is a 1.77% variance, inside the lower-of-2%/$50 band, so not a defect (clause 3). Tax of $473.25 recomputes exactly at the 7.5% vendor rate (clause 5); no credit memos outstanding (clause 9). Net payable $6,783.25 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

defects: Price variance outside tolerance and uncured: invoiced $154.00/EACH vs PO $145.00/EACH (+6.21%, allowance $2.90 under clause 3)
rows.rationale: Quantities match exactly (80 EACH ordered, received, invoiced) and no UOM conversion is needed. The unit price is $154.00 against a PO price of $145.00 — a 6.21% increase, far outside the clause 3 band (lower of 2% / $50.00 = $2.90). The only supporting document is a unilateral supplier price notice from Kestrel's billing team; it is not from or countersigned by an authorised buyer (Dele Fashanu, Priya Raman), so clause 3.1 does not cure it. Single defect, so no clause 11 escalation: hold for buyer action at $0.00.

Invoiced $93.28/EACH is exactly +6.00% over the PO's $88.00, outside the 2% band, but cured under clause 3.1: authorised buyer Dele Fashanu (vendor.json authorised_buyers) approved up to 6% on PO-4405, conduit line only, in writing. Receipt GR-7705 confirms 60 EACH received against 60 ordered and invoiced (clause 4), and tax of $419.76 matches the recomputed 7.5% exactly (clause 5). No defects; $6,016.56 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

defects: Quantity shortfall: 100 EACH invoiced, only 60 EACH received (GR-7706, balance of 40 on backorder)
rows.rationale: Receipt GR-7706 records 60 of 100 EACH received, with 40 on backorder. Clause 4 resolves the quantity dispute in favour of the receipt: short-pay on 60 EACH at the matching PO price of $9.50 = $570.00 net, plus recomputed 7.5% tax (vendor.json) = $42.75, gross $612.75. The tax reduction is a consequence of the quantity correction, not an independent tax discrepancy, so only one defect exists and clause 11 escalation is not triggered. Approver AP_CLERK per clause 10.

defects: Suspected duplicate: all five clause 8 conditions met against paid prior invoice NW-9912
rows.rationale: Clause 8: prior invoice NW-9912 (PAID) is the same vendor after name normalisation, same PO-4407, identical gross $3,225.00, 19 days apart, and neither invoice carries a service period, so clause 8.1 does not rescue it. The single line matches the PO and receipt exactly, meaning this is a re-billing of goods already invoiced and paid. Reject; payable $0.00 (clause 12).

March retainer matches the blanket SERVICES PO exactly (1 MONTH @ $4,800.00); no goods receipt is expected (clause 1). The prior INV-3221 shares vendor, PO and amount but covers a distinct, non-overlapping February service period, so it is a legitimate recurring charge, not a duplicate (clause 8.1). Tax recomputes to $360.00 exactly at 7.5% (clause 5), no credit memos, payable $5,160.00 → AP_CLERK (clause 10).

Line 1 matches PO and receipt exactly at 150 EACH @ $18.00 (clauses 3, 4). The $380.00 expedited freight line is a permitted non-PO charge: contract clause 6.2 allows pass-through of expedited carrier charges up to $500.00, the receipt notes production requested overnight freight, and $380.00 is under the ceiling (policy clause 6, not a defect per 11.1). Recomputed tax at 7.5% on $3,080.00 is $231.00, matching the supplier exactly (clause 5). No credit memos; net payable $3,311.00 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clauses 9-10).

defects: Tax overcharge: supplier billed $744.00 tax (12%) on net $6,200.00; correct tax at vendor rate 7.5% is $465.00, a $279.00 overcharge
rows.rationale: Price and quantity match exactly (200 EACH received per GR-7710 at $31.00/EACH, PO price identical), so clauses 3 and 4 are clean. The single defect is tax: recomputed at the vendor's 7.5% rate the tax is $465.00, not the invoiced $744.00 (clause 5) — supplier overcharge, so short-pay the corrected gross of $6,665.00. No credit memos (clause 9); one defect only, so no escalation (clause 11). Threshold puts approval with AP_CLERK (clause 10).

Contract clause 4.2 fixes EUR 1.00 = USD 1.10 for invoices dated 1 Jan–31 Mar 2026, so the PO price of EUR 210.00/EACH normalises to USD 231.00 — exactly the invoiced price (policy clauses 7 and 3, zero variance; conversion is normalisation, not a defect). Receipt GR-7711 confirms 40 EACH received against 40 ordered and invoiced (clause 4), and tax at the vendor's 7.5% recomputes to USD 693.00, matching exactly (clause 5). No non-PO lines, no credit memos; net payable USD 9,933.00 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

defects: Over-delivery beyond 5%: PO 100 EACH vs received/invoiced 118 EACH (+18%, tolerance 5 EACH) — clause 4
rows.rationale: Unit price matches the PO exactly ($7.40/EACH, no UOM difference), but the supplier shipped a full carton: 118 EACH received against a PO quantity of 100, an 18% over-delivery well beyond the 5% tolerance in clause 4. That is a single quantity defect, so no escalation applies (clause 11); hold pending receiving/buyer action with payable $0.00 (clause 12).

PO-4413 is a SERVICES PO, so the absent goods receipt is expected and not a defect (clause 1). Price and quantity match the PO exactly (clause 3), recomputed tax at the vendor's 7.5% rate equals the billed $562.50 (clause 5), no prior invoices so no duplicate risk (clause 8) and no open credit memos (clause 9). Net payable $8,062.50 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

defects: Quantity shortfall: 1200 CASE invoiced vs 1050 CASE received (150 cases short per GR-7714) — clause 4
Tax discrepancy: supplier billed $3,240.00 (9%) vs recomputed $2,362.50 at the 7.5% vendor rate on the corrected net of $31,500.00 — clause 5
rows.rationale: UOM normalises cleanly at 25 EACH/CASE (vendor.json pack size, confirmed by the PO description): 30,000 EACH @ $1.20 = 1,200 CASE @ $30.00, exactly the PO price (clause 2, 3 — not a defect). Receipt GR-7714 shows only 1,050 CASE received, so pay on received quantity: $31,500.00 net (clause 4). Recomputed tax at 7.5% is $2,362.50, not the $3,240.00 billed, so gross corrects to $33,862.50; netting open credit memo CM-2026-014 ($1,500.00) gives $32,362.50 (clauses 5, 9). Two defects and a net payable above $25,000 both trigger clause 11 escalation, with CONTROLLER approval per clause 10.

defects: Quantity shortfall on line 4 (Gland Plate): 25 EACH invoiced vs 20 EACH received per GR-7715 — clause 4
Tax discrepancy: supplier billed $609.84 (9% of its net) vs recomputed $463.20 at the 7.5% vendor rate on the corrected net of $6,176.00 — clause 5
rows.rationale: Line 2 reconciles exactly once normalised (40 CASE @ $24.60 = 480 EACH @ $2.05, clause 2) and line 3's $45.80 vs $45.00 sits inside the $0.90 band (clause 3) — neither is a defect. Two defects remain: line 4 was part-shipped (20 of 25 received, so payable at 20 × $120.00 = $2,400.00, clause 4) and the supplier applied a 9% tax rate instead of the 7.5% vendor rate. Corrected net $6,176.00 + $463.20 tax = $6,639.20; two defects force ESCALATE_HUMAN under clause 11 with this recommended payable (AP_CLERK band, clause 10).

defects: Price variance outside tolerance and uncured: invoiced $4,075.00/EACH vs PO $4,000.00/EACH, a $75.00 per-unit excess against an allowance of $50.00 (lower of 2% and $50.00)
rows.rationale: Quantities match exactly (2 EACH ordered, received on GR-7716, invoiced) and tax at the vendor's 7.5% rate is exact at $611.25, so the only issue is price. The unit price is $75.00 above the PO price, and the clause 3 band is the LOWER of 2% ($80.00) and $50.00, so the variance exceeds tolerance. No correspondence exists in the case file from an authorised buyer referencing PO-4416, so clause 3.1 cannot cure it. Single defect, so no clause 11 escalation; hold for buyer action.

defects: Price variance outside tolerance and uncured: invoiced $19.60/EACH vs PO $18.00/EACH (+8.89%, allowance $0.36 under clause 3); the copper surcharge was approved only by Femi Okonkwo (Warehouse Supervisor), who is not an authorised buyer, so clause 3.1 is not satisfied
rows.rationale: Quantities match exactly (500 EACH ordered, received per GR-7717 and invoiced), so the only issue is price. The approval email is from Femi Okonkwo, a warehouse supervisor not listed in vendor.json authorised_buyers, and the only buyer-level approval on file (Dele Fashanu) is expressly limited to PO-4405, so clause 3.1 does not cure the variance. Single defect, so clause 11 escalation is not triggered: hold for buyer action.

defects: Unauthorised surcharge: non-PO delivery and handling line of $640.00 exceeds the $500.00 cap in clause 6, so the contract clause 6.2 pass-through is not permitted
rows.rationale: Line 1 matches the PO and receipt exactly (6 EACH @ $410.00, GR-7718) and tax of $232.50 equals 7.5% of net, so those are clean. The decisive issue is invoice line 2: a non-PO 'Delivery and handling, oversize drums' charge of $640.00. Contract clause 6.2 permits passing through oversize carrier cost, but clause 6 of the policy also requires the charge be $500.00 or less; at $640.00 it fails, making it an unauthorised surcharge -> HOLD_PRICE_VARIANCE with payable $0.00. Single defect, so no clause 11 escalation.

defects: Tax undercharged: supplier billed $65.00 tax on net $1,300.00; correct tax at vendor rate 7.5% is $97.50, a $32.50 shortfall (clause 5)
rows.rationale: Price and quantity match exactly (400 EACH @ $3.25 ordered, received on GR-7719 and invoiced), so clauses 3 and 4 are clean. The only defect is tax: vendor.json rate 7.5% on the $1,300.00 net gives $97.50, but the supplier billed $65.00 — an undercharge, so per clause 5 the higher recomputed total of $1,397.50 is paid and flagged. Single defect, so no clause 11 escalation; AP_CLERK approves under clause 10.

No credit memos; payable $1,793.75, AP_CLERK band (clauses 9–10).

No open credit memos; $4,300.00 falls in the AP_CLERK band (clause 10).

defects: Quantity shortfall: 60 EACH invoiced but only 52 EACH received (GR-7724; 8 kits damaged in transit and refused at the dock)
rows.rationale: Price matches PO exactly ($320.00/EACH, clause 3) and no UOM conversion applies. The receipt shows only 52 of 60 kits accepted, so under clause 4 the payable is computed on the received quantity: 52 × $320.00 = $16,640.00 net, plus recomputed tax at the vendor's 7.5% rate = $1,248.00, giving $17,888.00. The supplier's $1,440.00 tax was correct for the invoiced quantity, so this is a single defect (the shortfall), not a separate tax discrepancy — clause 11 escalation is not triggered. No credit memos outstanding; clause 10 places $17,888.00 with AP_MANAGER.
